_comment: One rule, two languages. `cases` is run by BOTH frontend/src/utils/splits.test.ts and backend/tests/unit/test_split_predicate.py. A rule changed on one side only fails on the other. `backend_only` holds cases the frontend cannot express — see its own comment.

cases.note: a single leg is a valid split shape
a split with no lines is broken, not balanced

_backend_only_comment: Sub-cent amounts. Transaction.amount is Numeric(19,4), so the backend can hold and must reject these; the editors work in integer cents and round them to the nearest cent before they are ever compared, so the frontend cannot reproduce the case at all. Do not 'fix' the frontend to four decimal places to make these run there — the rounding happens at input, long before checkSplit sees it.

backend_only.note: the 0.001 tolerance used to accept this, and IntegrityService then flagged it forever
